title: Array and String Boundary Errors; Preventing Buffer Overflows
learningObjectives: Identify out-of-bounds reads and writes in array and string code.
Explain how off-by-one errors and missing null terminators cause memory defects.
Calculate required buffer capacity including terminator space.
Use checked length calculations before copying or appending data.
Apply boundary-focused tests and compiler diagnostics to reduce memory-safety risks.

understand.concept: An out-of-bounds access reads or writes outside the valid elements of an array object. Common causes include incorrect length calculations, off-by-one loops, missing null terminators and unbounded input. Such accesses have undefined behavior in C and can cause crashes, data corruption or security vulnerabilities. Prevention requires explicit capacity accounting, valid indices and careful API contracts.
understand.whyItMatters: This knowledge helps reason about C data representation, object bounds and valid memory access.
understand.analogy: Think of memory objects as labelled storage and pointers as typed references to that storage.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy does not replace C's formal pointer, lifetime and object-access rules.

explain.narrative:
## 1. Array bounds

For an array with N elements, only indices 0 through N-1 designate elements. An index equal to N is one past the last element and cannot be dereferenced. C does not automatically check array bounds at run time.

## 2. String capacity

A string with L data bytes requires at least L+1 char elements to include the terminating null character. When appending, calculate the existing length, incoming length and terminator space without overflowing the size calculation.

## 3. Validate before writing

Before copying or appending, prove that the destination has enough capacity. Do not rely on strcpy or strcat to discover the destination size; they do not receive that information. Reject, truncate or dynamically allocate according to an explicit policy.

## 4. Read safely

Use bounded input such as fgets and check its result. Detect overlong lines and handle the remaining input. A bounded read does not remove the need to validate the content.

## 5. Test boundaries and diagnose

Test empty input, the largest accepted input, one byte too many, exact-fit capacity and missing terminators. Compile with strong warnings and, where available, use address and undefined-behavior sanitizers during testing. Tools support prevention but do not replace correct bounds reasoning.

examples.title: Check capacity before copying
examples.explanation: sizeof source includes its null terminator. The capacity check therefore includes the complete string representation.

examples.title: Validate an index before access
examples.explanation: The index is checked against count before subscripting. The function also validates pointers before dereferencing them.

practise.guidedTask: Implement a small C program that checks array indices and string destination capacity before access or copying. Test exact-fit, empty and oversized cases.
practise.independentTask: Review a program with an off-by-one loop and an unsafe string copy. Identify the exact invalid access, calculate the required capacity, fix the defects and add boundary tests.
hints: Write down the exact array length and valid index range.
Include null terminator space when working with C strings.
Check function preconditions and return values.
Pass array lengths explicitly when a function needs them.

questions.prompt: For a string with 10 data characters, how many char elements are needed?
questions.explanation: The array needs ten data elements plus one null terminator.

questions.prompt: What is an out-of-bounds array access in C?
options: Reading or writing outside the valid elements of the array
questions.answer: Reading or writing outside the valid elements of the array
questions.explanation: An array access must designate an element within the object's bounds.

questions.prompt: Why are strcpy and strcat risky when capacity is unknown?
options: They do not know the destination array's capacity
They always append a terminator twice
questions.answer: They do not know the destination array's capacity
questions.explanation: The caller must ensure sufficient destination storage.

questions.prompt: Which test is especially useful for a bounded input buffer?
options: Input exactly at capacity and one byte beyond the accepted limit
questions.answer: Input exactly at capacity and one byte beyond the accepted limit
questions.explanation: Boundary tests reveal truncation and capacity-handling defects.

questions.prompt: What does an address sanitizer help detect during testing?
options: Some invalid memory accesses such as out-of-bounds operations
questions.answer: Some invalid memory accesses such as out-of-bounds operations
questions.explanation: Sanitizers detect classes of runtime memory errors but cannot prove all code correct.
